answer: The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, slashed on a failed audit, rewards vest against future work. Reaching the shale of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the reef of a task receipt, and the kernel is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce.
